item.title: ChatBots Are Killing People!
item.description:
With all the recent discussion of the potential catastrophic impacts AI might cause in the future, we’re losing track of the significant harms it is already causing right now. In this episode, Cal goes deep into a serious and tragic topic that he recently learned about in a panel discussion about children and technology. He has an urgent warning for parents that has implications for all of us as well.

item.title: An Insider's Guide to AI Doom
item.description:
The conversation around AI harms has become incredibly heated in recent weeks. But it's also incredibly confusing. In this short explainer episode, Cal walks through the three major categories of beliefs around AI in the current moment and helps explain who belongs where and how they all relate to each other. If you're trying to keep up with AI news you have need to learn this framework.

item.title: A Single Sheet of Paper Can Fix Your Overwhelm
item.description:
One of the more debilitating experiences in our current digital world is the sense of being trapped in relentless, reactive, busyness. This “whirlwind” can separate you from both ambition and presence, leaving you feeling flat and fried. In this episode, Cal discusses a simple trick he deploys when he finds himself in this state. It requires only a single sheet of paper.

item.title: Mathematicians Just Proved How to Prevent AI Brain Rot
item.description:
How do we stop from becoming so reliant on LLMs that we lose our ability to think. A new paper explores answers based on an unlikely source: rigorous mathematical models. In this episode, Cal explains the paper and its conclusions, arguing that once you cut through its complexity it yields a useful way of thinking about our current AI moment.

item.title: “Rogue” AI Is Not Inevitable. It’s a Choice.
item.description:
A lot of attention has been paid recently to examples of AI going “rogue.” What’s missing from this discussion, however, is a more detailed explanation of what specific types of systems are causing problems. Taking a closer look at this problem reveals an issue that’s much more narrow and much more avoidable than some of the frontier labs would like you to believe.

item.title: The Normie’s Guide to Thinking About Tech
item.description:

item.title: Why Are Harvard Students Lining Up for This “Brutal” Class?
item.description:
Two years ago, The Atlantic featured a distressing story about elite college students who could no longer read books. Last week, The Wall Street Journal offered some hope that things are getting better. An article by Pamela Paul described how Harvard’s ‘brutal’ humanities course, Hum 10, which requires students to read one hefty book per week, has become extremely popular. In this short episode, Cal explores why this is happening and what it tells us about how best to resist our would-be digital overlords.

item.title: Phones Stole Our Lives. We Investigated How to Reclaim Them.
item.description:
It’s becoming increasingly clear that the negative impact of phones on our lives is larger than we’d like to admit. Maybe it’s time to move beyond tips and hacks to explore more serious interventions. But what would these look like? In this episode, Cal dispatches correspondent Dale Davidson on a world-spanning investigation of some of the more extreme solutions people have deployed to reclaim their lives from their devices.

item.title: AI Broke Work. This 100-Year-Old Idea Can Fix It.
item.description:
The theoretical capability of AI tools seems to be expanding rapidly. At the same time, however, their practical impact in the office has been uneven. Why? In this episode, Cal journeys through the history of the idea of “efficiency,” from the 1750s through today, exploring why this concept explains AI’s workplace struggles and what approach might solve them.
